patch_description:
The original program failed validation for several reasons: (1) it returned an empty list as `column_orderings`, giving the evaluator no valid per-row column permutations; (2) its recursive group-value reordering mutated row order/columns inconsistently (e.g. appending an `original_index` column and renaming columns mid-recursion, producing shapes and label mismatches); (3) it used expensive per-node pandas `Counter(df.stack())` and thread pools over `itertuples` rows, causing timeouts; (4) its objective (squared field lengths, adjacent grouping) did not match the actual character-Trie reuse metric.

Fix: complete rewrite inside the block. It serializes each cell exactly as the evaluator does (NaN→"", str(value)), precomputes per-column factorized codes and length-weighted repetition scores once, builds three cheap candidate per-row column orderings (global frequency-ranked order, a conditional partition tree that splits rows on the highest length-weighted repetition column, and a length-free frequency variant), scores each candidate with the true ideal Trie objective (sort serialized row strings, sum adjacent LCPs via binary search on prefix slices so comparisons run in C), and returns the best. The returned DataFrame keeps original row order, original column labels, and exact original cell values (object dtype), with per-row orderings that are permutations of the column labels. col_merge is honored via the parent `merging_columns`; all other API parameters are accepted and bounds (row_stop/col_stop/early_stop/distinct_value_threshold) cap tree depth and branching.
